title: The Three Musketeers, Part 2
author: Alexandre Dumas
summary: Na primeira parte, o jovem d'Artagnan ficou amigo de Athos, Porthos e Aramis e salvou a honra da rainha ao trazer de Londres as joias que o Cardeal Richelieu queria usar contra ela. Agora o Cardeal quer vingança, e sua arma mais perigosa é Milady de Winter, uma mulher linda, inteligente e sem piedade, que guarda um segredo terrível. Entre a guerra no cerco de La Rochelle, intrigas na Inglaterra e a busca por Constance, os quatro amigos enfrentam o inimigo mais cruel de suas vidas.

chapters.title: Lost and Found
paragraphs: A few days after the ball, d'Artagnan received a short letter from Constance. “Come to Saint-Cloud tonight at ten o'clock,” it said. “Wait in front of the little house near the river.” He was there at nine, full of hope. But ten o'clock came, then eleven, then midnight, and Constance did not come.

At last, an old man came out of a little house nearby. He was trembling with fear. “Sir,” he said, “I saw everything. A carriage arrived an hour ago. Some men took a young woman and put her inside. She was screaming. There was a tall man with them, a man with a scar on his face. And there was a little fat man too, who pointed at her.”
“Rochefort and her own husband!” said d'Artagnan. “They have kidnapped her again!”
He went to Monsieur de Tréville, who told him to be patient. “The Cardinal has her,” said the captain. “You cannot fight the Cardinal alone. Go and find your friends first. You need them.”

So d'Artagnan and Planchet took the road to Calais again. At Chantilly, they found Porthos in bed at the inn. He had won his duel, but he had slipped and hurt his knee. He was too proud to say this, so he told everyone that he had been badly wounded. He also had no money to pay the innkeeper, and he was eating and drinking with Mousqueton as if he were a king.

In the next town, d'Artagnan found Aramis in a little room, with two priests. Aramis was wearing black clothes and talking about religion. “I am leaving the army,” he said sadly. “I am going to become a priest.” But then d'Artagnan gave him a letter that had arrived from his secret lady. Aramis read it, and his face changed completely. He threw his religious books into the air and laughed. “Bazin! Bring me my sword and my musketeer's coat! The world is beautiful again!”
At Amiens, the innkeeper was very nervous when d'Artagnan asked about Athos. “He is still here, sir,” he said. “He is in the cellar. He has been there for twelve days.”

After the fight, Athos had escaped from his attackers and shut himself in the inn's wine cellar with a pistol. Nobody dared to open the door. When d'Artagnan called him, Athos came out. He was dirty, but he was smiling. Behind him, the cellar was full of empty bottles. He had drunk almost all the wine in the house.
“D'Artagnan!” he said. “I am happy to see you. Come, let us have breakfast. I am a little hungry.”
That night, Athos drank more wine. He sat with his head in his hands, and he looked older and sadder than ever before. D'Artagnan told him about his love for Constance, and how he had lost her.
“Love!” said Athos bitterly. “Love is a game, and the one who wins always loses. Listen, my friend. I will tell you a story about love.”

chapters.title: Athos's Story
paragraphs: “There was once a young count in my part of France,” began Athos. “He was rich and noble, the lord of the whole region. When he was twenty-five, he fell in love with a girl of sixteen. She was as beautiful as an angel. She had golden hair and blue eyes, and she was very clever. She lived with her brother, a young priest, in a small village. Nobody knew where they came from, but nobody cared, because she was so lovely.”
D'Artagnan listened in silence.

“The count could have taken her as a lover,” Athos went on, “but he was an honest man. He married her. He made her the first lady of the region, and she lived in his castle like a queen. He was happy, because he thought she loved him.”
Athos drank another glass of wine.

“One day, they were riding together in the woods. Her horse fell, and she fell too. She did not move. The count ran to help her. Her dress was too tight and she could not breathe, so he cut it open with his knife. And on her shoulder...” Athos stopped. His face was white. “On her shoulder he saw a fleur-de-lis, the mark of the lily. It was burned into her skin with hot iron.”
D'Artagnan was shocked. “The fleur-de-lis! But that is the mark that the executioner puts on criminals!”

“Yes,” said Athos. “The angel was a thief. She had stolen from a church. And the young priest was not her brother. He was her lover, and he had helped her. The count was all-powerful on his lands. He had the right to judge. So he tied her hands behind her back, and he hanged her from a tree.”
“Oh, God! Athos!” cried d'Artagnan. “That is murder!”
“Yes, it was murder,” said Athos quietly. He put down his glass. “And it cured me of beautiful women, of poetry and of love. That is the end of my story.”
“And the count?” asked d'Artagnan. “What happened to him?”

Athos did not answer. He only stood up and went to bed. But d'Artagnan understood. The young count was Athos himself. That was why he never spoke about his past, and that was why his eyes were always sad.
The next morning, Athos pretended that he did not remember anything. “I drank too much last night,” he said. “I always tell stupid stories when I drink. Forget it.”
But d'Artagnan never forgot it.

The four friends returned to Paris together. They needed money for new horses and equipment, because the King was preparing for war. The Protestants of La Rochelle, a port on the west coast, had closed their gates against the King. The Duke of Buckingham was going to send English ships to help them. Soon the whole army would leave Paris for La Rochelle.

Each of the friends found money in his own way. Porthos visited a rich old lady who was in love with him. Aramis received a big bag of gold from his secret lady. Athos sold a beautiful horse that the Duke of Buckingham had given to d'Artagnan, and they shared the money. And d'Artagnan himself was about to meet a woman who would change all their lives.

chapters.title: The Woman with Golden Hair
paragraphs: One Sunday, d'Artagnan was walking near a church when he saw a beautiful lady getting into her carriage. She had pale golden hair and blue eyes. He knew her at once. It was the woman from Meung, the woman who had stolen the studs from Buckingham. It was Milady!

He followed her carriage on horseback. On the road, she stopped to speak to an English gentleman, and they began to argue. D'Artagnan rode up to them. “Sir,” he said to the Englishman, “are you making this lady angry?”
“I don't need your help,” said Milady coldly, and her carriage drove away.

The Englishman was Lord de Winter, Milady's brother-in-law. He was proud, and he did not like d'Artagnan's question. So the two men agreed to fight a duel, with three friends each. D'Artagnan brought Athos, Porthos and Aramis. When the duel ended, d'Artagnan had knocked Lord de Winter's sword out of his hand. He could kill him, but he did not.

“You are a true gentleman,” said Lord de Winter, as he got up. “You have saved my life. Let us be friends. Come, I will introduce you to my sister-in-law, Lady de Winter. She is the widow of my brother.”

So d'Artagnan began to visit Milady's house. She was charming and clever, and she always received him with a smile. But d'Artagnan noticed that sometimes, when her brother-in-law was not looking, her eyes were as cold as ice. Lord de Winter was rich, and if he died, all his money would go to Milady's little son.

Milady had a pretty young maid called Kitty. One evening, Kitty stopped d'Artagnan on the stairs. “Sir,” she whispered, “you must stop coming here. My mistress does not love you. She is in love with another man, the Count de Wardes. And she hates you, because you hurt him at Calais.”
She showed him a letter from Milady to de Wardes. D'Artagnan read it and became angry. Milady wanted to know where de Wardes was, because she wanted to see him alone, at night.

Kitty was in love with d'Artagnan, so she agreed to help him. She stopped giving Milady's letters to de Wardes. Instead, she gave them to d'Artagnan, and he wrote the answers himself, as if he were de Wardes.
“Come to me tomorrow night,” wrote Milady. “But come in the dark, so that my servants don't see you.”
The next night, d'Artagnan went to Milady's room in the dark. She thought that he was de Wardes. She was soft and loving, and she gave him a beautiful sapphire ring.
“Keep it, my love,” she said. “And there is something I want you to do for me. There is a young Gascon called d'Artagnan. He has insulted me. I want you to kill him.”
D'Artagnan's blood went cold. He left her room before the sun came up, without saying who he was.
The next day, he showed the sapphire ring to Athos. Athos looked at it, and he went white.
“Where did you get this ring?” he asked.
“From Lady de Winter. Why?”
“Because it was my mother's ring,” said Athos slowly. “I gave it to my wife.”

chapters.title: The Mark on the Shoulder
paragraphs: D'Artagnan should have stopped there. But he was young, and he wanted to win against Milady. He wrote her a rude letter, as if it came from de Wardes. “I am sorry, madame,” it said, “but I have too many other ladies to see. I don't have time for you.”

Milady was furious. That evening, when d'Artagnan came to visit her as himself, she smiled at him more sweetly than ever. “You are a brave man, d'Artagnan,” she said. “If somebody insulted me, would you help me?”
“Of course, madame. Who has insulted you?”
“The Count de Wardes,” she said. “Kill him for me, and I will be yours.”

That night, in her room, d'Artagnan decided to tell her the truth. He thought she would laugh. “Milady,” he said, “I must confess something. De Wardes never received your letters. It was I who came to your room last week. It was I who wrote that rude letter. Please forgive me.”

Milady's face changed completely. It was no longer beautiful. It was white and terrible, like the face of a wild animal. She jumped at him and tried to hit him. He held her arm, and her thin nightdress tore at the shoulder. There, on her white skin, d'Artagnan saw a small mark. It was a fleur-de-lis.
“Good God!” he cried.
Milady knew that he had discovered her secret. She took a knife from the table and attacked him. “You will die!” she screamed. “Nobody who knows my secret can live!”
D'Artagnan ran out of the room, with Milady behind him. Kitty pulled him into her little room and locked the door. Milady was hitting the door with her knife and shouting for her servants.
“Quick, sir!” said Kitty. “Put on my dress and my cap. They are looking for a man, not a girl.”

A few minutes later, a strange young woman with big boots and a sword under her skirt ran through the streets of Paris. When d'Artagnan arrived at Athos's house, Grimaud opened the door and almost dropped his candle. Athos, who was always calm, started to laugh. It was the first time in years that anybody had heard him laugh like that.
But when d'Artagnan told him everything, Athos was not laughing any more.
“Describe her to me,” said Athos. “Golden hair? Blue eyes, very light? A little scar near the eye? About twenty-six years old?”
“Yes, yes, yes. All of that.”
“And the fleur-de-lis on the left shoulder?”
“Yes.”
Athos covered his face with his hands. “Then it is her. She did not die on that tree. She is alive. She is my wife, Anne de Breuil. And now she is Lady de Winter.”
“She married again?” asked d'Artagnan.

“Of course. She married Lord de Winter's brother, and he died very suddenly. Do you understand what kind of woman she is now, d'Artagnan? She is a devil. She will never forget what you did tonight. She will try to kill you. Be very careful.”

D'Artagnan helped Kitty to escape from Paris, so that Milady could not punish her. Then, a few days later, he left for La Rochelle with his regiment. He was glad to go to war. On the battlefield, at least, he knew who his enemies were.

chapters.title: The Siege of La Rochelle
paragraphs: La Rochelle was a strong city by the sea, with high walls all around it. The King's army was camped outside the walls, and the siege had already begun. The Cardinal wanted to win the war quickly, because the English ships could arrive at any moment to help the Protestants. So he gave an order to build a great wall of stone in the sea, to close the port.

D'Artagnan was not with his friends. He was a guard of Monsieur des Essarts, and the three musketeers were still in Paris with the King. One evening, d'Artagnan was walking alone near the camp when he saw two guns pointing at him from behind a wall. He threw himself on the ground, and the bullets flew over his head.

A few days later, he went out with his soldiers to look at the enemy's walls. In the fight, somebody shot at him again, but not from the enemy side. It was from behind him! He caught one of the attackers. The man was terrified.
“Who paid you?” asked d'Artagnan, with his sword at the man's throat.
“A lady, sir. A beautiful lady with golden hair. She paid us a hundred gold coins to kill you.”
“Milady!” said d'Artagnan.

Soon after, the King and the musketeers arrived at the camp, and d'Artagnan was very happy to see his friends. One day, a present of fine wine arrived for d'Artagnan. The letter with it said that it was from his three friends. But when he met them, they said that they had not sent anything. They ran back to d'Artagnan's tent. There they found Brisemont, a poor soldier who worked for d'Artagnan. He had drunk a glass of the wine, and he was dying in terrible pain.
“Poison,” said Athos quietly. “This is Milady's work again.”

One night, Athos, Porthos and Aramis were riding near a little inn called the Red Dovecote. Suddenly they met a group of riders. The leader was wearing a large hat and a long cloak. It was the Cardinal himself! He did not want to be recognized, so he asked the musketeers to go with him as his guards.

At the inn, the Cardinal went upstairs to meet someone. The three musketeers waited in the room below. But Athos discovered that, through an old pipe in the wall, he could hear every word of the conversation upstairs. The Cardinal was speaking to a woman. It was Milady.

“You will go to London,” said the Cardinal. “Tell the Duke of Buckingham that if he sends his ships to La Rochelle, I will tell the King everything about him and the Queen. And if he does not listen...”

“If he does not listen,” said Milady, “someone must kill him. There are many crazy men in England who hate the Duke. I will find one. But I want something too, Your Eminence. I want d'Artagnan dead. And I want a paper, signed by you, that says I acted for France. Then nobody can arrest me for what I do.”
The Cardinal wrote a few words on a piece of paper and gave it to her. Then he left. When everyone had gone, Athos went upstairs alone.
Milady was sitting by the fire. When she saw his face, she screamed. “The Count de La Fère!”
“Yes, madame,” said Athos. “I thought you were dead. You thought I was dead. But here we are.” He pointed his pistol at her head. “Give me the paper the Cardinal has just signed.”
Milady saw in his eyes that he would shoot. She gave it to him. Athos read it: “It is by my order and for the good of the State that the bearer of this paper has done what he has done. Richelieu.”
“Now go to England,” said Athos. “But if you touch d'Artagnan, I will kill you.”

chapters.title: Breakfast Under Fire
paragraphs: The next morning, the four friends wanted to talk about Milady. But in the camp there were spies everywhere, behind every tent and under every window. “I know a place where nobody can hear us,” said Athos.

There was an old bastion in front of the camp, called Saint-Gervais. It was very near the enemy's walls. Athos made a bet with some officers. “My friends and I will eat our breakfast in the bastion of Saint-Gervais,” he said, “and we will stay there for one hour, whatever the enemy does.”

So the four friends, with Grimaud carrying a basket of food and wine, walked to the bastion. They sat down among the dead bodies of soldiers and began to eat. Soon a group of enemy soldiers came to attack them. The friends picked up the old muskets that were lying around and fired. The enemy ran away. Then they went on with their breakfast and their conversation.
“Milady has gone to England to kill Buckingham,” said Athos. “We must warn him.”
“But if we warn the English Duke, we are traitors to France,” said Porthos.
“Then let us warn Lord de Winter,” said d'Artagnan. “He is my friend. We can tell him that his sister-in-law is a murderer, and that she is coming to London. He can watch her.”
“And Constance?” asked d'Artagnan sadly. “Where is she?”
“Leave that to me,” said Aramis with a small smile. “I have a friend, a lady who is very close to the Queen. She will help us find out.”

A second group of enemy soldiers came, bigger than the first. This time Athos had an idea. There was an old wall at the top of the bastion that was ready to fall. The four friends pushed it with all their strength, and it fell down on the attackers. Then they finished their wine. The hour was over, and they walked slowly back to the camp, while the bullets were flying round their heads.

The whole army was waiting for them, and the soldiers were shouting with joy. Even the Cardinal heard about it. “Those four men are the bravest in the army,” he said to Tréville. “I want them to work for me.” But Tréville only smiled. He knew that the four friends would never work for the Cardinal. To thank them, the Cardinal let d'Artagnan join the musketeers. At last, he had the blue coat!

The friends sent their two letters. A few days later, an answer came from Aramis's friend. The Queen had saved Constance from the Cardinal's prison. Now she was hidden in a convent, in the little town of Béthune, in the north of France. D'Artagnan's heart jumped with joy.
Meanwhile, Milady's ship arrived at Portsmouth, in England. She was smiling as she came off the ship. But a young officer was waiting for her with some soldiers.
“Lady de Winter?” he said politely. “Please come with me.”
He took her in a carriage to a lonely castle by the sea. There, Lord de Winter was waiting for her.

“Welcome, dear sister,” he said coldly. “I know everything about you. I know that you killed my brother. I know that you want to kill the Duke. You will stay here, in this room, until a ship takes you far away, to the other side of the world. And this young officer, John Felton, will guard you. He is an honest man, and he hates evil. You cannot buy him with money or with smiles.”
Milady said nothing. But her eyes were already studying the young officer's face.

chapters.title: Felton
paragraphs: John Felton was a young Puritan. He was very religious, he prayed many times every day, and he hated the Duke of Buckingham. Many Puritans believed that Buckingham was a bad and selfish man, and that he was sending English soldiers to die in a war for his own love affairs.

Milady understood all this quickly. For the first two days, she did not eat. She lay on her bed, pale and silent. Then she began to pray, loudly and with passion, in the Puritan way. Felton stopped outside her door to listen. She sang religious songs with a beautiful, sad voice. Little by little, the young officer started to feel sorry for her.

One day, when Felton came into her room, she was holding a knife. “Don't stop me!” she cried. “I want to die!” Felton took the knife from her hand. After that, he came to see her every day. He wanted to save her soul.
Then Milady told him her story. Of course, it was all lies, but she told it with tears in her eyes, and he believed every word.

“When I was young,” she said, “a powerful lord fell in love with me. I refused him, because I was a good and religious woman. So he kidnapped me, and he gave me a drug and took my honour. And when I said that I would tell everyone, he paid the executioner to burn a mark on my shoulder, the mark of a criminal. Then nobody would ever believe me.” She opened her dress a little and showed him the fleur-de-lis. “Look! This is what he did to me.”
“Who is this man?” asked Felton. His face was white with anger.
“It is the Duke of Buckingham,” whispered Milady.
Felton fell on his knees. “I will avenge you,” he said. “I swear it before God.”

On the night before the ship came to take Milady away, Felton helped her to escape. She climbed down a rope from her window in the storm, and he took her to a small boat. Then Felton rode to Portsmouth, where the Duke of Buckingham was preparing his ships for La Rochelle.

Buckingham was in his room when Felton came in. The young man asked him to sign a paper and set Lady de Winter free. Buckingham refused. Suddenly Felton pulled out a knife and pushed it into the Duke's side, up to the handle.
At that moment, a messenger was arriving from France. Lord de Winter ran in, too late. Buckingham was lying on the floor, dying.
“Is there a letter from the Queen?” whispered the Duke.
The messenger gave it to him. The Queen had written that she was worried about him, and that he must be careful. Buckingham smiled and held the letter against his heart. Then he died.
Lord de Winter looked at Felton. “Why did you do it?” he cried.

But Felton was not listening. He was looking out of the window at the sea, where a small French ship was sailing away. He understood, too late, that Milady had used him. She had never cared for him. She was free, and he would die for her.

chapters.title: The Convent at Béthune
paragraphs: Milady arrived in France and sent a message to the Cardinal. He told her to wait for him at a quiet convent in the town of Béthune. There, the nuns welcomed her kindly. She told them sad stories about the Cardinal's enemies, and they believed she was a poor, good lady.
“We have another young lady here,” said the Mother Superior. “She is hiding too. She is very lonely. Perhaps you could be friends.”
The young lady came in. She was pretty, with dark hair and blue eyes. Her name was Constance Bonacieux.

The two women talked for hours. Constance had no idea who this beautiful stranger was. Soon she began to talk about the man she loved. “He is so brave,” she said, with shining eyes. “He went to London for the Queen. His name is d'Artagnan. He is going to come and take me away from here.”
Milady smiled sweetly. But inside, she was burning with hate and joy. Now she had a perfect way to hurt d'Artagnan. She could take away the woman he loved.
That evening, Rochefort came to the convent with news from the Cardinal. Milady talked to him quietly. “Send a carriage for me tomorrow,” she said. “I will bring the girl with me.”
The next morning, a letter arrived for Constance. It was from d'Artagnan. “Be ready,” he wrote. “We are coming for you today.” Constance was very happy. She showed the letter to her new friend.

“Today?” said Milady. “Oh, my poor child. I am afraid it is a trick! The Cardinal knows everything. Those men will not be your friends. They will be the Cardinal's men, dressed as musketeers. You must come with me. My carriage is waiting. I will hide you somewhere safe.”

Constance was frightened, and she did not know what to do. Then they heard the sound of horses on the road. Milady ran to the window. She saw four riders in blue coats, and she recognized d'Artagnan at the front. Her face went white.
“Quick!” she said. “They are coming! We must go now!”
But Constance was too weak with fear. Her legs would not carry her. Milady saw that there was no time. She quickly poured a glass of wine, and she dropped a red powder from her ring into it.
“Drink this,” she said. “It will give you strength.”
Constance drank. Then Milady ran out of a back door, jumped into the carriage and was gone.
A moment later, d'Artagnan ran into the room. “Constance! Constance! It's me!”
Constance smiled at him. “You came,” she said. “I knew you would come.” But then she fell into his arms. Her face was white, and her body was shaking with pain.
Athos looked at the empty glass and smelled it. His face became very dark. “Poison,” he said.
“Who gave you this?” cried d'Artagnan. “Tell me!”
“The lady... my friend... Lady de Winter,” said Constance. She looked into d'Artagnan's eyes. “I love you,” she whispered. Then she closed her eyes and died in his arms.
D'Artagnan gave a terrible cry and fell to the floor beside her, like a dead man.
At that moment, an Englishman came into the room. It was Lord de Winter. He had followed Milady from England. He looked at the dead young woman, and at the four friends.
“I am too late again,” he said sadly. “She killed my brother. She has killed the Duke of Buckingham. And now she has killed this poor girl.”
Athos stood up. His face was calm and terrible. “Gentlemen,” he said, “we will find her. And then we will judge her.”

chapters.title: The Man in the Red Cloak
paragraphs: Athos sent the servants out along every road. Before the night came, Planchet returned with news. Milady was hiding in a small, lonely house near the town of Armentières, by the river Lys.
Athos did something strange then. He went alone to a house outside the town, and he came back with a tall man in a red cloak. The man wore a mask over his face, and he did not say a word.

It was a dark, stormy night when they arrived at the lonely house. Through the window, they could see Milady sitting near the fire. D'Artagnan broke the window with his pistol, and Athos came in through the door. Milady screamed and tried to run, but there was nowhere to go. The five men stood in front of her, with the man in the red cloak behind them.
“What do you want?” she cried.
“We want to judge you,” said Athos. “D'Artagnan, you speak first.”

“I accuse this woman of poisoning Constance Bonacieux,” said d'Artagnan, “and of trying to poison me. Instead of me, my poor soldier Brisemont died. I accuse her of paying men to shoot me in the back.”

Lord de Winter spoke next. “I accuse this woman of killing my brother with poison. I accuse her of the death of the Duke of Buckingham. And I accuse her of the death of John Felton, who will die because of her lies.”

Then Athos spoke. His voice was very quiet. “I married this woman when she was a young girl. I gave her my name and my love. Then I found out that she was a thief, with the mark of a criminal on her shoulder. I tried to punish her, but she lived.”
“Who can prove that I have that mark?” said Milady proudly. “Who can prove that I am a criminal? Who put that mark on me?”
The man in the red cloak stepped forward. He took off his mask. Milady looked at his face, and she screamed in horror.
“The executioner of Lille!” she said.

“Yes,” said the man. “Many years ago, this young woman lived in Lille. My brother was a young priest there. She made him fall in love with her, and she persuaded him to steal the gold from his church. They ran away together. When they were caught, my brother went to prison, and I put the mark on her shoulder myself, because that was my job. But she escaped. My brother escaped to find her, and he became her ‘brother’ in a little village in the north. Then she married a rich young count. When the count found out the truth, my brother killed himself from shame. I have been looking for this woman ever since.”
Everyone was silent. Outside, the wind was screaming and the rain was falling.
“What is your sentence?” asked Athos. “D'Artagnan? Lord de Winter? Porthos? Aramis?”
Each of them answered with the same word: “Death.”

They took her down to the river. Milady cried and begged and promised them gold. She tried to charm them with her beautiful eyes, as she had charmed so many men. But nobody listened. When they arrived at the bank, d'Artagnan felt sorry for her for a moment. “I can't,” he said, and he turned away. But Athos stood firm.
The executioner took her across the river in a small boat. On the other side, under the dark sky, he raised his sword. Then he wrapped her body in his red cloak and threw it into the deep water.
“Let God's justice be done,” said Athos. The friends took off their hats and stood silently by the river for a long time.

chapters.title: The Lieutenant
paragraphs: The four friends rode back to the camp at La Rochelle. On the way, at an inn, a tall man with a scar came in with some soldiers. It was Rochefort.
“Monsieur d'Artagnan,” he said, “I have an order from the Cardinal. You are under arrest. Give me your sword.”
D'Artagnan gave it to him without a word. His friends went with him to the Cardinal's house. They waited outside, ready to fight the whole army if necessary.
The Cardinal was sitting at his table. He looked at d'Artagnan with his cold, clever eyes.

“Young man,” he said, “you are accused of many things. You have worked with the enemies of France. You have given secrets to the English. And you have killed a lady who worked for me, Lady de Winter. Do you know what that means? It means death.”
“Your Eminence,” said d'Artagnan calmly, “who accuses me? A woman who was a thief, a poisoner and a murderer. She was judged by five men, and she is dead.”

He told the Cardinal the whole terrible story of Milady's life and crimes. The Cardinal listened in silence. When the story was finished, he said, “Even so, you had no right to judge her. You will be punished.”

“I knew you would say that, Your Eminence,” said d'Artagnan. “And so I have brought this.” And he gave the Cardinal a piece of paper. It was the paper that Athos had taken from Milady at the Red Dovecote.
The Cardinal read it: “It is by my order and for the good of the State that the bearer of this paper has done what he has done. Richelieu.”
For a long time, the Cardinal said nothing. He looked at the paper and then at the young man. D'Artagnan was ready to die. Then, slowly, the Cardinal tore the paper into small pieces.
“I am lost,” thought d'Artagnan.

But the Cardinal took a new sheet of paper and began to write. When he finished, he gave it to d'Artagnan. “Here,” he said. “I took one paper from you, and I give you another. The name is empty. You can write it yourself.”
D'Artagnan looked at the paper. It was an order that made somebody a lieutenant in the King's Musketeers.
“You are a brave man, d'Artagnan,” said the Cardinal, with a small smile. “I prefer to have you as a friend, not an enemy. Go now.”
D'Artagnan ran to his friends. First he offered the paper to Athos. “It is yours,” he said. “You are the most noble of us.”

“No,” said Athos. “For Athos it is too much. For the Count de La Fère it is too little. Keep it, my friend.” Porthos did not want it either, because he was going to marry his rich lady and leave the army. And Aramis gave it back too. “I am going to become a priest,” he said, and this time he was serious.
So d'Artagnan wrote his own name on the paper. He became a lieutenant of the Musketeers. Soon after, La Rochelle fell, and the King's army returned to Paris.

The friends went their separate ways, but they never forgot each other. D'Artagnan fought three duels with Rochefort and wounded him three times. After the third duel, the two men shook hands and became friends. D'Artagnan often thought of Constance, and he felt sad. But he had found his place in the world, and three friends who would always be at his side.
All for one, and one for all.
